prompt_text: What is the best tanning salon in Pleasanton CA?
answer_verbatim:
I don’t have live web access to check current reviews, so I can’t name a single “best” salon in Pleasanton right now. I can, however, help you find the best one for your needs and give tips so you can pick confidently. Quick questions first:

- Are you looking for spray tanning or UV tanning (tanning beds)?  
- Do you want the cheapest option, the highest-rated luxury salon, or something in-between?  
- Any location constraints (near a particular neighborhood or address)?

How to find the best one (fast)
- Search Google Maps or Yelp for “spray tan Pleasanton” or “tanning salon Pleasanton.” Sort by rating and read recent reviews (last 6–12 months).  
- Check Facebook and Instagram for before/after photos and how they respond to customers.  
- Look for salons that show staff certifications and list the brands they use (spray solution brand, bed manufacturer).

What to look for in reviews and listings
- Cleanliness and up-to-date equipment (for beds: age/brand of lamps; for spray: airbrush vs booth, solution brand).  
- Staff professionalism and safety practices (goggles, wipe-downs, ventilation).  
- Consistency (many photos of real clients, repeat customers).  
- Clear pricing and package deals; cancellation/no-show policies.  
- How they handle patch tests or consultations (especially for spray tans or first-time users).

Questions to ask a salon before booking
- What types of tanning do you offer (stand-up spray booth, airbrush, UV beds)?  
- What brand of spray solution do you use and does it contain DHA only or bronzers too?  
- How old are your tanning lamps and how often are they serviced/replaced?  
- Do you require or offer a patch test for spray tans?  
- Are appointments required and what is your cancellation policy?  
- Do you offer memberships or packages and what’s the cost per session?

Safety tips
- For spray tans: follow pre- and post-tan instructions carefully (exfoliate before, avoid sweating for recommended time after).  
- For UV tanning: limit sessions, follow salon guidance, and consider alternatives (spray) to reduce skin cancer risk.  
- If you have skin conditions or are on photosensitizing medications, consult a doctor first.

If you tell me whether you want spray or UV, and any location or budget preferences, I’ll give a tailored list of likely top options and wording you can paste into Google/Yelp to find current, highly rated salons near you.
